detailed_rationale:
Cupid Ltd is a global manufacturer and exporter of male condoms, female condoms, lubricants and IVD/diagnostic kits, WHO/UNFPA pre-qualified for both male and female condoms (the first company in the world to hold both), exporting to over 125 countries with a large institutional/government-tender revenue base (governments, NGOs, global health agencies). The company has been on an extraordinary growth run: Q3 FY26 (Dec 2025) revenue was up 101.7% YoY to Rs 93.49 crore with PAT up 196.3% to Rs 32.83 crore; Q4 FY26 (Mar 2026) revenue stepped up further to about Rs 120 crore with net profit of about Rs 36 crore and operating margin improving to 31%. Q1 FY27 is tracking to exceed Rs 150 crore, one of the strongest quarters in company history, and management has raised FY27 revenue guidance from Rs 600 crore to over Rs 660 crore. This is backed by real capacity and market-access investments, not just sentiment: a new land acquisition at Palava, Maharashtra will add about 770 million male condom units and 75 million female condom units of annual capacity; the company is developing premium nitrile female condoms (a higher-margin category with limited global competition); it has commenced a long-term supply agreement with PFSCM (Netherlands), a major global health-procurement body; and the board has approved the company's first international manufacturing facility, in Saudi Arabia. The stock has re-rated enormously alongside this -- per the quant screen, returns are +102% over 3 months, +143% over 6 months, +798% over 1 year and +1,111% over 2 years, taking market cap to roughly Rs 29,000-31,000 crore.

The balance sheet is reasonably clean (borrowings of about Rs 56 crore against total liabilities of Rs 553 crore per the latest available screener data; the quant screen's D/E of 0.12x and interest coverage of 39x tell the same story) and returns on capital are strong and improving (ROE about 27.3% and ROCE about 33.5% on the most recent trailing data, versus the quant screen's slightly staler 16.4%/17.0% -- the trend is clearly upward as margins expand). However, the valuation has moved far ahead of even this genuinely strong operating story: trailing PE is now in the 266-290x range across sources and the stock trades at roughly 70x book value -- both extreme by any standard, growth-stock or otherwise. Additional flags worth noting: the company has a history of volatile working capital (working-capital days improved to 119 from 151, but have peaked as high as 570 days in prior periods) consistent with lumpy institutional/tender collections; and despite consistent, growing profits, the company pays no dividend, which is a reasonable capital-allocation choice given the capacity build-out underway but is worth flagging as a governance/payout-policy observation. Promoter holding is 46.24% with no evidence of pledging.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen carries this as Hold, and its own scoring already flags the tension here: an extremely low value_score (9.38, i.e., very expensive) and a growth_divergence_flag (1-year growth of 95.6% running far ahead of the 3-year CAGR of 33.9%, i.e., a recent sharp acceleration) sit alongside very strong quality and growth scores. My own research confirms the growth is real and multi-year capacity/contract-backed, not purely narrative -- but the valuation (266-290x trailing PE, ~70x book) has run so far ahead that it would take flawless, uninterrupted execution for several years to grow into this multiple, on a revenue base that is meaningfully institutional/tender-driven and therefore inherently lumpier and more competitively contestable (on price, in government tenders) than a typical branded consumer franchise. I cannot rescue this further (quant is already Hold) and I am not permitted to force a Sell against a quant Hold -- but I genuinely believe the valuation extremity here is a real analytical tension worth a portfolio-manager look rather than a routine Hold, so I am escalating while leaving the recommendation at Hold per the rules.
summary: Cupid Ltd makes male and female condoms, lubricants and diagnostic kits, and has become one of the fastest-growing names in its space -- revenue and profit have roughly doubled year-on-year for several quarters running, backed by real capacity expansion, a new premium female-condom product line, a long-term supply deal with a major global health-procurement agency, and a first overseas manufacturing plant planned in Saudi Arabia. The business itself looks genuinely stronger than a year ago. But the share price has moved even faster than the business -- up roughly 8-11x over one to two years -- and now trades at an extremely rich valuation (over 260 times trailing earnings, around 70 times book value) that leaves very little room for anything to go wrong in what remains a government/institutional tender-driven revenue base. We rate it a Hold, but are flagging the valuation extremity for portfolio-manager review rather than treating it as a routine call.
positive_para: Genuinely accelerating, capacity- and contract-backed growth: revenue and profit have both roughly doubled YoY for multiple consecutive quarters, margins are expanding (31% operating margin in the latest quarter), and the growth is underwritten by real investments -- a large Palava capacity expansion (+770 million male and +75 million female condom units annually), a premium nitrile female-condom line in a low-competition niche, a long-term PFSCM (Netherlands) supply agreement, and a first international manufacturing plant planned in Saudi Arabia -- on a clean balance sheet (modest debt, ROCE about 33.5%).
negative_para: The valuation has moved far beyond even this genuinely strong operating story -- trailing PE of roughly 266-290x and price-to-book of about 70x leave essentially no margin of safety, and the quant screen's own growth_divergence_flag shows the current pace (95.6% YoY) is a sharp acceleration versus the 3-year trend (33.9% CAGR), a pattern the skill explicitly warns against extrapolating at face value. Revenue remains meaningfully institutional/government-tender driven, a model with historically volatile working capital (peaks of 570 days) and inherent price competition in public tenders; the company also pays no dividend despite sustained profitability, which is defensible given the capacity build-out but adds to the list of things requiring continued flawless execution to justify today's price.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a trailing PE in the 266-290x range and roughly 70x book value, the market is pricing in several more years of 30%+ compounding with margin expansion and no execution missteps -- a very high bar for a business whose revenue base is meaningfully institutional/tender-driven and whose own growth rate only recently accelerated from a much smaller base. Even crediting genuine hypergrowth (this qualifies for the >=25% tier: confirmed new capacity, a signed long-term international supply agreement, and a new overseas plant are real, not narrative), a PEG-style read of ~270x PE against ~28-30% forward growth is still extremely rich by any reasonable growth-at-a-price standard. On the required ROE/dilution disclosure for >=25% growth calls: ROE is about 27.3% on the latest trailing data (and rising), and the growth so far looks largely non-dilutive -- funded by modest incremental debt (~Rs 56 crore borrowings) and retained earnings rather than a large equity raise -- though the new Saudi plant and Palava capacity build-out will require continued capital and bear watching for future dilution.
escalation_reason: Valuation is now so extreme (trailing PE ~266-290x, P/B ~70x) that even crediting a genuine hypergrowth-tier forward estimate (~28-30%) implies a PEG multiple near 9-10x -- far beyond any normal growth-at-a-reasonable-price threshold. The underlying business is genuinely improving (real capacity expansion, a signed long-term PFSCM supply agreement, a new Saudi Arabia plant, margins rising to 31%), so this is not a case of fabricated momentum, but the revenue base remains meaningfully institutional/government-tender driven, with historically volatile working capital (peaks of 570 days) and no dividend despite sustained profits. I believe there is a genuine, defensible case that this should be a Sell on valuation grounds alone despite the strong operating momentum -- the quant framework's own growth_divergence_flag and rock-bottom value_score (9.38) already signal this tension. Given the asymmetric-override rule I cannot convert this quant Hold to Sell myself, so flagging for the portfolio manager to personally weigh valuation extremity against operating momentum.
